title: Billing Office Explainer: Pricing a Level-Change Segment on an Assisted Living Respite Stay
content:
A level-change segment on an Assisted Living Respite Stay under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement charges every re-leveled night at the nightly rate locked at booking and adds the care increase billed for the re-leveled nights.

## Terms of the charge

- **The re-leveled nights** are the nights of the stay's latest level-change adjustment credit.
- **The nightly rate locked at booking** is the locked nightly rate recorded on the stay.
- **The care increase per re-leveled night** is the published nightly rate of the stay type on record less the nightly rate locked at booking.
- **The care increase billed per re-leveled night** is that care increase in full, and it is billed on every re-leveled night.
- **The level-change segment** is the re-leveled nights times the nightly rate locked at booking, plus the nights on which the care increase is billed times the care increase billed per re-leveled night, rounded half up to the cent once, on the final total.

Taken together, the full care increase is billed for every re-leveled night, so the level-change segment equals the re-leveled nights times the published nightly rate of the stay type on record.

## Worked statement (hypothetical stay)

A hypothetical Assisted Living Respite Stay booked as Standard Care is locked at 239.00 a night; the stay type on record is now the Assisted Living Respite Stay (Enhanced Care), whose published nightly rate is 284.00, and the latest level-change adjustment credit states 9 nights.

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Re-leveled nights at the locked rate: 9 times 239.00 | 2,151.00 |
| Care increase per re-leveled night: 284.00 less 239.00 | 45.00 |
| Care increase billed: 9 nights times 45.00 | 405.00 |
| Level-change segment: 2,151.00 plus 405.00 | 2,556.00 |

The same figure follows directly as 9 times 284.00, that is 2,556.00.

## Points of reading

- The rate that every re-leveled night carries first is the locked nightly rate of the stay, not the rate of the stay type on record.
- The published nightly rate read is the one of the stay type on record at the time of the segment.
- Rounding is applied once, to the final total, never to a line.
